thought.text: The grep matched minified React internals. Let me check the CSS-inlining more precisely by searching for distinctive CSS content in the bundle.

reasoning_content:
The grep hit minified React internals (because they contain "insertBefore"). Not the pattern I was looking for. The important point is: `dist/index.html` has no `<link rel="stylesheet">` pointing to the widget's own CSS file — the only stylesheets are the portal's chrome (fpo-*.css) and include.css (the preview banner). The widget's CSS should be inlined into the JS bundle (the guide says "a single javascript file with css inlined"). Let's do a more targeted check: look for CSS injection patterns like `styleSheet` or `.sheet`, or check whether there's a large CSS string inside the JS. Let me try grepping more precisely for typical inlined CSS markers.

Actually, as a simpler and more targeted check: `grep -c 'eltern' assets/index-BefVnHEI.js`, or look for CSS custom properties like `--` variables, or the presence of Tailwind-generated class definitions like `.eg-` inside the JS. Let's search for a distinctive CSS selector string inside the bundle.

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "cd /workspace/dist; grep -o 'styleSheet[^,;]\\{0,40\\}' assets/index-BefVnHEI.js | head -5; echo ---; grep -c 'Elterngeldrechner' assets/index-BefVnHEI.js; grep -o 'eg-[a-z-]\\{3,\\}:[^;]\\{0,30\\}' assets/index-BefVnHEI.js | head -3; echo ---; grep -o 'tailwind' assets/index-BefVnHEI.js | head -1; grep -c 'background-color' assets/index-BefVnHEI.js", "stylesheets": "true", "summary": "Search dist bundle for inlined CSS evidence"}
